title: Lexer Internals
concept: The lexer transforms raw source text into a token stream — the first stage of compilation. Understanding it reveals how XIOM reads your code.
why: Every syntax error message starts in the lexer. Understanding tokenization helps you interpret errors, write tooling, and even contribute to the compiler.
tips: The lexer runs before any other phase — syntax errors here have the simplest fix
Token positions (line, col) are stored for error reporting — essential for good diagnostics
Whitespace and comments are skipped by the lexer — they never reach the parser
Look-ahead (peeking the next character) handles multi-character tokens like '->' and '=='
common_mistakes: Confusing lexer errors with parser errors — syntax errors say 'unexpected character'
Assuming the lexer validates semantics — it only recognizes tokens, not their meaning
Forgetting that lexer errors abort compilation — the parser never sees a broken token stream
